title: Incident #107: Pre-Auth Stanza Injection & XML Entity Attacks
solutionExplanation: Enforces pre-auth security gates and recursive XML entity escaping to neutralize injection attacks.

otpDocCards.description: Recursively escapes &, <, and > characters into XML entities.
otpDocCards.complexityNote: Tail-recursive binary fold in O(N) time.

mentalModelCheck.question: In Incident #107, what allowed unauthenticated attackers to inject fake admin commands into the session?

options.label: The connection state machine processed incoming <message> stanzas before the client finished SASL PLAIN authentication, and lacked an XML character escape loop.
options.explanation: Failing to reject pre-auth stanzas and neglecting to escape &, <, > characters allows authentication bypass and XML injection.

options.label: The server used MD5 password hashing instead of SHA-256.
options.explanation: The bug was architectural: pre-auth stanza dispatch and unescaped entity strings.

options.label: The Erlang runtime crashed on large payloads.
options.explanation: The BEAM handles large payloads effortlessly; this was an application security failure.

options.label: The client used an expired TLS certificate.
options.explanation: The incident occurred over plain C2S TCP streams without pre-auth state validation.

incidentAlert.symptom: Unauthenticated sockets can inject arbitrary stanzas and corrupt client XML streams with unescaped characters.
incidentAlert.impact: Privilege escalation and client disconnection cascades across the cluster.
incidentAlert.diagnosticClue: Connection state machine processed stanzas before SASL auth, and lacked XML entity escaping.
